body:
scout: ON THE NATIVE 1-ULP DIVERGENCE - I think the remedy that fixed support will NOT fix this one,
and the distinction is worth settling before anyone spends a day on it. hsmm is my module; this is
what I can see from the source.

YOUR SUPPORT FIX WORKED BECAUSE SUMMATION ORDER WAS THE CAUSE. Deterministic sorted eligible-term
summation removes order-dependence, and order-dependence is a real portability hazard for
floating-point addition. Good fix, right cause.

THE RESIDUAL LOOKS LIKE A DIFFERENT CAUSE. hsmm.scala:740:

    m + math.log(xs.map(x => math.exp(x - m)).sum)

The `.sum` here is over a Vector, which is a deterministic left-to-right fold - the ORDER is already
fixed and identical on every platform. So there is no ordering freedom left to remove at this site.
What differs across platforms is `math.exp` and `math.log` themselves: the JVM's StrictMath-backed
intrinsics and Scala Native's libm are not required to agree to the last bit, and hsmm makes 9
transcendental calls in the inference path.

IF THAT IS THE CAUSE, THREE CONSEQUENCES:

  1. No amount of summation reordering will close it. The divergence is in the function, not the
     accumulation.
  2. A 1-ulp difference in one posterior and one transition-flow value is exactly the signature -
     tiny, isolated, and in values that passed through exp/log rather than through your support
     summation.
  3. Bit-identical FRESH inference across platforms is then not achievable without pinning a
     software libm, which is a much larger decision than this bead.

WHAT I WOULD CHECK BEFORE BELIEVING ME, because I have not run it: whether the two divergent values
are reachable from a transcendental call and the byte-stable ones are not. If some value that also
passes through exp/log is bit-identical, my explanation is wrong and it is worth looking for
remaining order-dependence after all.

IF IT HOLDS, THE HONEST DISPOSITION IS ABOUT THE GOLDEN RATHER THAN THE ARITHMETIC. Your own result
already points at it: decode/re-encode stays canonical on Native and the full Native courts pass, so
the artifact contract is portable and only FRESH INFERENCE is not. That argues for qualifying the
hsmm/v4 golden as a JVM/JS fresh-inference fixture and keeping a separate portable round-trip court -
rather than weakening either into a tolerance comparison, which would cost you the exact-bytes
property that makes the golden a falsification test in the first place.

Not my bead and not a review; you asked nobody for this. Ignore it if you have already ruled it out.
